correctness.rationale: A length-n circular presentation uses exactly n ordered edges including closure, with a one-letter word giving a single loop. Balanced nonzero multigraphs are realized by Euler circuits exactly when their active undirected support is connected. The three net differences are a single signed triangle flux; together with the three opposite-pair minima and the three independent loop counts it parametrizes each balanced matrix uniquely. Summing gives F(z), where the zero flux is counted once. The excluded types are two active loop singletons and an inactive vertex, an active reciprocal pair and a loop singleton, or three active loop singletons, in addition to the zero matrix. Each correction has the stated multiplicity. At z=1 the principal constants are 1/12 for the order-seven balanced pole and 3/2 for the order-four disconnected pole, giving 1/8640 and 1/4 in the respective coefficients and 2160 in their ratio. At z=−1 the numerator 1+z^3 cancels one of the three factors from 1−z^2, leaving a double pole, which corrections with at most a simple pole cannot remove. Primitive third-root poles also persist; the pole orders and locations yield degree six and minimal eventual quasiperiod six. Selecting one word per attainable matrix gives the maximum deterministic zero-error count. A fresh weak-composition enumeration of unconstrained nine-entry tables, filtering for balance and connectivity, matched coefficients through n=14 (3960 at n=14), and all its retained matrix sets matched a direct circular-word scan through n=9.
residual_risks: Finite confirmation only covers the stated ranges; the all-length results follow from the exact series and pole analysis. The alphabet is labeled and there is no restriction to words using all three labels.

evidence: Let q=B_1=1/(1−z) and let E_m be the exact full-label connected component series, including the inactive one-label graph in E_1. For m=2 the published partition identity gives E_2=B_2−q^2=z^2/((1−z)^2(1−z^2)). For m=3 it gives E_3=B_3−3E_2 q−q^3. Restoring inactive labels yields positive-length T=E_3+3E_2+3(q−1).

Therefore B_3−1−T=3E_2(q−1)+3(q−1)^2+(q−1)^3, exactly the three frozen corrections. Its largest pole is (3/2)(1−z)^−4, so the leading coefficient 1/4 and ratio constant 2160 follow directly. Eq. (40) prints the leading coefficient for P_n(3).
